dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Hi Nikhil, thanks for having us. We're going through the organization department by department for the DPDPA privacy assessment. We started with HR yesterday and today we're kicking off with Customer Care. This first session is really about understanding what your department does, how it's structured, what data comes in and goes out, and identifying the areas we'll need to dive deeper into.

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Sure, welcome. I've heard about the assessment from the leadership team. About time we did this. We handle a lot of customer data here and I've had my own concerns about how we manage it.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: That's a great starting point. Let's begin with the structure. How is the Customer Care department organized?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: The department has about 45 people in total. Broadly we have three functions. First is the call centre operation — inbound customer calls. These are the agents who sit on the phones all day. They handle queries, service requests, complaints, the whole range. Second is the Compliance Calling team — they make outbound calls to customers for verification and hygiene checks. That's a smaller team, about 8 people. Third is the Quality team — they audit calls, monitor call quality, and train new agents.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: And reporting structure?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: All three teams report to me. I have a Team Lead for the call centre — that's Farhan. Compliance Calling is managed by Deepa. Quality is handled by Smita. I report to the Chief Operating Officer.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Got it. Let's talk about the channels. How do customers reach you?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Three channels. Toll-free number — that's the primary one, accounts for probably 80% of our interactions. WhatsApp — we have a business WhatsApp number that customers can message. And email — customers can email us at a generic customer care email address, but email volume is relatively low compared to calls.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Let's start with the toll-free number. Walk me through what happens when a customer calls.

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: The call first hits our IVR system. We use Ameyo — it's our IVR and call management platform. The IVR has two paths depending on whether the customer is calling from a registered mobile number or an unregistered number.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: How does the system know if it's a registered number?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Ameyo is integrated with Salesforce. When a call comes in, the system checks the caller's number against our customer database in Salesforce. If it matches a registered mobile number, the customer gets the full service IVR menu. If it doesn't match, they get a limited menu.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: That's an important integration. Let me understand both paths. First, unregistered numbers.

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: For unregistered callers, the IVR gives three options. Option 1 is for new loan inquiries — the call gets transferred to the Sales team. We don't handle that. Option 2 is for DSA-related queries — DSA means Direct Selling Agent. If they select DSA, they get two sub-options: new code requests and payment-related inquiries. In both cases, a case gets created in Salesforce automatically and our team resolves it within 2 business days, then we share the update with the client.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: And option 3 for unregistered numbers?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Option 3 is if it's an existing customer calling from a different number — not their registered mobile. In that case, we ask them to call back from their registered number. We don't verify identity over phone for unregistered numbers. That's a security policy.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Good. That's actually a solid privacy control. Now registered numbers.

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: For registered callers, Ameyo pulls up the customer profile from Salesforce and shows it on the agent's screen before they even pick up. The caller ID match is the first level of identification. Then the IVR gives six options:

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: When a customer selects an option and connects with an agent, what does the agent see on their screen?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: The agent gets a Salesforce screen with the customer's profile. That includes — — customer name, loan account number, registered mobile number, email address, loan product type, sanctioned amount, outstanding principal, EMI amount, next due date, payment history, overdue status if any, co-applicant details if there is one, and the branch that originated the loan. Plus any previous case history — past complaints, queries, service requests.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: That's a significant amount of data on screen. Are agents trained on data protection? Like, are they told not to read out the full loan details unless the customer confirms their identity?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: The caller ID match from Ameyo is considered sufficient identification. If the call is from the registered mobile number, we assume it's the customer. We don't do an additional KYC on the call. Which, now that I think about it, could be an issue — someone else could be using the customer's phone.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: That's worth flagging. The registered number alone may not be adequate identity verification for disclosing financial data. Let's move on. You mentioned case categories?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Yes. Every interaction gets logged in Salesforce as a case. There are four case categories:

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: For complaints involving bribery, what data is captured?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Customer name, loan account number, the name of the employee or branch being complained about, a detailed description of the incident, any supporting evidence if the customer has it — sometimes they send WhatsApp screenshots or email threads. All of this goes into Salesforce and is flagged for the Ethics team.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Those complaints could contain very sensitive information. Who has access to them in Salesforce?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: That's a good question. All customer care agents can see all cases in the system. There's no restriction based on case category. So technically, a regular agent could open a bribery complaint case and see the details. The Ethics team has their own view, but the cases aren't hidden from Customer Care.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: That's a significant access control gap. Bribery complaints could include whistleblower-like information and sensitive personal allegations. Access should be restricted.

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Agreed. I've raised this before but Salesforce configuration hasn't been updated.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: We'll include it as a priority recommendation. Let me ask about the TAT you mentioned. What's the turnaround time for different case types?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Queries are resolved on the call, so real-time. For Service Requests and Customer Issues, the TAT is 48 hours. Complaints have a 24-hour acknowledgment and 7-day resolution target. There's an escalation matrix defined in our SOP — it goes from Team Lead to me to the COO depending on severity and age of the case.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: The SOP — is that the "V2 Customer Care SOP" document?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Yes, that's the one. I can share a copy.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Please do. Last question for this session — what about the option 5, Loan Closure. You mentioned the call goes to a Retention team?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Right. If a customer calls to close their loan or requests a foreclosure, the call is transferred from our team to the Retention desk. Retention is technically under the Business team, not under Customer Care. They try to convince the customer to continue the loan. If the customer insists on closure, Retention processes it. From our side, we just transfer the call and log a case.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: And the customer's data — their account details, their stated reason for wanting to close — that's visible to both Customer Care and Retention?

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Yes, through Salesforce. Retention has access to the same customer records we do.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Nikhil, this has been very productive. We've got a solid picture of the department structure, communication channels, case management, and some important data access concerns. In the follow-up sessions, I want to go deeper into the Compliance Calling process, the Ameyo-Salesforce integration, call recordings, and data retention.

dialogue.speaker: Nikhil Joshi
dialogue.text: Sounds good. Farhan or Deepa can join the next sessions. They'll have more operational detail than me on some of those topics.

dialogue.speaker: Rohan Desai
dialogue.text: Perfect. We'll coordinate scheduling. Thanks, Nikhil.
